content: Rifampin interacts with various drugs by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which accelerates the metabolism of these drugs, leading to reduced plasma levels and diminished therapeutic effects. Below are specific examples of these interactions and recommendations for clinical management: 1. Enzalutamide: Rifampin reduces enzalutamide levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, increase the enzalutamide dose from 160 mg daily to 240 mg daily. Revert to the original dose if the strong CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued. 2. Erdafitinib: Rifampin decreases erdafitinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, separate administration by at least 6 hours before or after P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 3. Ergotamine: Rifampin reduces ergotamine levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Erlotinib: Rifampin decreases erlotinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate): Rifampin reduces erythromycin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Estradiol and other estrogens (conjugated synthetic, estropipate, ethinyl estradiol): Rifampin reduces estrogen levels, potentially compromising the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use non-hormonal contraceptives instead. 7. Etonogestrel: Rifampin decreases etonogestrel levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Etrasimod: Rifampin reduces etrasimod levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Everolimus: Rifampin decreases everolimus levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Fedratinib: Rifampin reduces fedratinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Felbamate: Rifampin decreases felbamate levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Felodipine: Rifampin reduces felodipine levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Fesoterodine: Rifampin decreases fesoterodine levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Fexinidazole: Rifampin increases fexinidazole levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Fineranone: Rifampin reduces fineranone levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Fludrocortisone: Rifampin decreases fludrocortisone levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Fosamprenavir: Rifampin reduces fosamprenavir levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Fosaprepitant: Rifampin decreases fosaprepitant levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Fostamatinib: Rifampin reduces fostamatinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Fruquintinib: Rifampin decreases fruquintinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Futibatinib: Rifampin reduces futibatinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Ganaxolone: Rifampin decreases ganaxolone levels. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose without exceeding the maximum daily dose. 23. Gepirone: Rifampin reduces gepirone levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Gilteritinib: Rifampin decreases gilteritinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Glasdegib: Rifampin reduces glasdegib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Rifampin reduces glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Hydrocortisone: Rifampin decreases hydrocortisone levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Hydroxyprogesterone caproate: Rifampin reduces hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Ibrutinib: Rifampin decreases ibrutinib levels by approximately 10-fold. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Idelalisib: Rifampin reduces idelalisib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Iloperidone: Rifampin decreases iloperidone levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 32. Indinavir: Rifampin reduces indinavir levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Infigratinib: Rifampin decreases infigratinib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Istradefylline: Rifampin reduces istradefylline levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Ivabradine: Rifampin decreases ivabradine levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 78. Olutasidenib: Rifampin reduces olutasidenib levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 79. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 84. Palovarotene: Rifampin reduces palovarotene levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 85.
